claims.statement: The whole build is one script chain - `tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc -p tsconfig.renderer.json && node scripts/copy-assets.mjs` - and the `dev`, `dev:panel` and `accept` scripts each run that build before starting Electron, so no launch path can start against a stale `dist`; `typecheck` and `test` are the only scripts that need no build.

The repository has no packaging or installer step: the application is run from the checkout as `electron .` with `dist/` as the only build product, which is why `main` points at a compiled file and every runnable path starts with a build.

The build uses no bundler: the renderer was moved (ticket 10, route b) to native ES modules loaded through the custom `deck-plugin://` scheme, so plain `tsc` output is directly runnable and relative specifiers keep their `.js` suffix; the earlier Vite plan never landed.

`tsconfig.json` compiles `src/main`, `src/preload` and `src/shared` as CommonJS (`module: commonjs`, `target: es2022`) into `dist` with `rootDir: src` and `strict`; it is the Electron main-process side that runs under Node's CommonJS loader, and it excludes the renderer and the tests.

`tsconfig.renderer.json` covers `src/renderer` and `src/shared` with `module: es2022` because the renderer never runs under Node: the page is loaded as `deck-plugin://app/index.html` and starts from `<script type="module" src="./main.js">`, and card entries are dynamically imported through the same scheme.

Serving the renderer as ES modules depends on two protocol facts: the `deck-plugin` scheme must be registered as privileged (`standard`, `secure`) before app ready, and the asset handler delivers only a MIME whitelist in which `.js`/`.mjs` map to `text/javascript` - anything else is answered 404 and the module fails to load.

Because `tsc` emits relative specifiers verbatim, renderer sources and card manifests must name their siblings with an explicit `.js` extension (`./plugins.js`, `./format.js`, `entry: "./card.js"`), unlike the extensionless imports in the CommonJS main process.

`src/shared` is included by both build projects and both write into `dist`, so `dist/shared/contract.js` is emitted twice and the renderer project (run second) leaves the ES-module form on disk; the main process nevertheless consumes that same file as a value through the single non-type import of the contract, `PLUGIN_CAPABILITIES` in `plugins/manifest.ts`, making the order of the two `tsc` invocations load-bearing.

`tsconfig.typecheck.json` extends the main config with `noEmit: true` and `rootDir: "."`, and includes `src/**/*.ts` plus `tests/**/*.ts`; since neither build project compiles the tests, it is the only program that type-checks the renderer and the offline suite together.

`scripts/copy-assets.mjs` copies exactly the assets `tsc` cannot emit: `src/renderer/index.html`, each `src/renderer/cards/<id>/plugin.json`, `src/main/icon-restore-watch.cjs` and `src/main/autostart.ps1`.

The copied non-TypeScript helpers are load-bearing siblings of compiled modules: `icon-restore-watch.cjs` requires `./icon-carry.js` from the same directory, and the compiled autostart module runs `powershell.exe -File path.join(__dirname, 'autostart.ps1')`, which is why the copy step targets `dist/main`.

A card directory without a `plugin.json` is not mountable: the manifest is copied rather than compiled, and the plugin host reads a directory with a missing or invalid manifest as an `error` entry under a sanitized fallback id rather than instantiating it.

Nothing in the build removes files from `dist` - `tsc` only emits, the copy script only writes, and `dist` is gitignored - so a deleted or renamed card leaves its previous `card.js` and `plugin.json` under `dist/renderer/cards`, where the built-in plugin root still discovers and mounts it; deleting `app/dist` by hand is the only cleanup path.

Electron's entry point is `dist/main/index.js`, and the renderer is delivered from `dist/renderer` as the protocol root (`RENDERER_ROOT` is `__dirname/../renderer`, its `cards/` subdirectory is the built-in plugin root, and the page URL is `deck-plugin://app/index.html`), so launching without a fresh build leaves the panel with nothing to load.

Other runtime paths are resolved relative to `dist/main`: the panel preload is `__dirname/../preload/index.js`, the data-plane worker module is `__dirname/dataplane.js` (forked with `utilityProcess.fork`), and the restore watcher is spawned from `__dirname/icon-restore-watch.cjs`.

Runtime mode is selected purely by `process.argv` at the top of `index.ts`: `--icon-restore` is a one-shot restore that exits without touching the instance lock, `--panel` boots the panel window, `--accept` runs the acceptance battery inside the same Electron app context with an empty `window-all-closed` handler, and no flag at all runs the outer supervisor.

The single-instance rule is a deliberate lock handoff: the supervisor requests the lock, releases it before spawning the panel child (a residual lock would make the fresh panel look like a second instance), and the `--panel` child takes it again and holds it for its whole life; a refused launch logs `single-instance-refused` and exits 0 in under 3 s while the running process receives `second-instance` and re-shows the panel.

`--accept` bypasses the single-instance lock by construction, because both lock branches in the entry dispatch are guarded by `!ACCEPT_MODE`; that is what lets real-machine acceptance run while a panel is already resident.

`bootPanel()` runs in a fixed order - load or generate config, apply the autostart decision, migrate the legacy usage log, start the kernel, await the first data-plane snapshot, install the protocol handler, create the window, wire bridge and host IPC, create the tray, then load the page - and the first-snapshot wait is capped at 15 s so a broken data plane cannot block the desktop.

The first run generates `app/config.json` next to `package.json` (`CONFIG_FILE` is `app.getAppPath()/config.json`), seeded from the current display geometry; invalid fields fall back to defaults with a warning instead of being silently accepted.

Runtime state (the placement store `layout.json`, the usage log directory) lives under Electron's `userData` rather than the code directory, and `userDataPath()` falls back to `LOCALAPPDATA/agent-deck-panel` when Electron is unavailable.

`DECK_EVENT_LOG` turns the main process into a best-effort JSONL evidence recorder (`fileEventLog`, appending `{t, ...event}` per line and swallowing write failures); it is unset in normal development runs and set to `accept/evidence/03-runtime-events.jsonl` by the acceptance battery for the panel processes it spawns.
Normal teardown is the tray menu item `退出面板` (`app.quit()`), after which the supervisor restores the desktop icons and exits; the panel itself has no window chrome and no taskbar entry to quit from.

A console kill (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break, closing the terminal) takes the supervisor and panel down together before any in-process restore hook can run, which is why the supervisor spawns the detached `icon-restore-watch.cjs` after hiding the icons, and why `npx electron . --icon-restore` is the documented self-help path.

The acceptance battery is a controller that spawns its own panels as `electron .` (the supervisor entry, so the whole spawn chain is under test) from the app root with `DECK_EVENT_LOG` set, and drives them through its own Win32 bindings instead of imported production modules.

`npm run accept` is not sandboxed: the battery hides and restores the native desktop icons (falling back to `--icon-restore` at teardown after killing the panel tree), backs up and restores `app/config.json` and the placement store in `userData`, injects real cursor movement and clicks, and writes its verdict log and screenshots into `app/accept/evidence/`; its process exit code is the verdict (0 pass, 1 fail, 2 crash).

The acceptance battery is hand-written plain JavaScript (`accept/battery.js` and `accept/lib/*`) that no project compiles and that `tsconfig.typecheck.json`'s `src`/`tests` include does not cover; `--accept` simply `require`s it at runtime, so its only verification is the run itself.

`npm test` runs `vitest run` with no configuration file against TypeScript sources imported directly from `src`, so the offline suite needs neither a build nor Electron; it also contains source-level guards that read repository files and fail when a boundary is crossed (the renderer and preload must not reach for `node:fs`, the search chain must not touch the usage log or hard-code URLs).

There is no watch or hot-reload mode: every launch script builds once and then starts Electron, nothing reloads the page when `dist` changes, so a source edit costs a full rebuild plus a relaunch - while protocol responses are served `cache-control: no-store`, so a relaunch always serves the freshly built assets.

The application and its acceptance harness are Windows-only: the Win32 layer loads `user32.dll` through koffi, autostart shells out to `powershell.exe`, and the harness captures screenshots with a DPI-aware PowerShell script.

The repository's parallel-development rule is one main checkout on `master` (the machine's autostart points at that checkout's `app/`) plus `feat/<slug>` worktrees under `D:\local_works\agent-deck-wt\<slug>`, and because the panel is single-instance parallel worktrees must not each keep a resident panel - real-machine verification uses `npm run accept`, whose acceptance mode bypasses the lock and can coexist with a running panel.

Deleting a remote branch requires explicit user confirmation beforehand, and without it branches in the gh repository that the user did not check out themselves must not be deleted; local `git branch -d` is unrestricted.
